title: Naikidevi Stops the Ghurid Road
subtitle: The Regent Who Barred the Western Gate
region: Kasahrada near Mount Abu, Patan and the Thar route
moral: Leadership is the courage to choose the ground before the battle begins.

sources.citation: Minhaj-i-Siraj Juzjani, Tabaqat-i-Nasiri, c. 1260 CE, trans. H.G. Raverty
sources.note: Independent Islamic account of the defeat near Nahrwala.

sources.citation: Sundha Hill inscription of the Jalor Chahamanas, 1262 CE, Epigraphia Indica, vol. 9
sources.note: Near-contemporary epigraphic evidence for Kirtipala and the victory at Kasahrada.

sources.citation: Kiradu inscription, 1178 CE, Epigraphia Indica series
sources.note: Contemporary context for Turushka military activity and temple repair.

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of Naikidevi on a fort wall, desert and distant army faint on the horizon

dialogue.text: In 1178, as Muhammad of Ghor drove toward Gujarat, a widowed regent named Naikidevi chose the ground where his road would end.

panels.shot: slow push-in from cityscape of Patan to throne hall interior

dialogue.text: Patan, capital of the Chaulukyas of Gujarat. King Ajayapala dead, his son Mularaja a child, the kingdom held together by one word on every grant and order: ‘Naikidevi, regent.’

panels.shot: tight mid-shot of Naikidevi at a council, angled from slightly below

dialogue.speaker: Messenger
dialogue.text: Devi, word from the north: a Turushka army has crossed the passes.

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder view from behind Naikidevi toward the map on the floor

dialogue.text: In distant Ghur, the Shansabani prince Muhammad had turned from Ghor to Ghazni, from Kabul to the plains. Now his men, the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri says, marched toward Nahrwala in Gujarat.

panels.shot: cut to a harsh landscape wide of the Thar route, caravan and riders in the distance

dialogue.text: The Kiradu inscription had already spoken of Turushka attacks, of temples damaged, of repairs that followed. Now a larger host advanced, not for a raid, but for the rich fields of Gujarat.

panels.shot: intimate close-up on Naikidevi’s eyes, lit by lamplight

dialogue.text: Later storytellers would picture her riding into battle with her child in her lap. The chronicles are quieter. They simply show a regent who held authority, and a decision she would not delay.

panels.shot: medium wide of court scene as she addresses feudatories, slightly elevated angle

dialogue.speaker: Naikidevi
dialogue.text: If we wait behind walls, we yield the roads. We will choose our ground.

panels.shot: montage-style wide showing different chiefs in their own domains receiving summons

dialogue.text: Inscriptions on Sundha Hill would later carve their names: Kirtipala, Kelhanadeva, Dharavarsha. The regent’s summons called not for a single champion, but for a coalition.

panels.shot: broad landscape shot of the Aravalli foothills near Mount Abu, early morning light

dialogue.text: Near Mount Abu, at Kasahrada, the land itself offered a weapon: tight passes, broken ground, flanks of stone. Here, Naikidevi’s coalition would meet the Ghurid road.

panels.shot: mid-shot of Naikidevi in a campaign pavilion, conferring with generals with map between them

dialogue.text: The Sundha inscription will praise the warriors who broke the Turushkas. The Tabaqat will recall a disastrous march. Between them we see her work: the choice of ground, the placing of men.

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of the Ghurid vanguard entering the constricted pass

dialogue.text: The Ghurid host, hardened by marches from the Oxus to the Indus, moved into the Kasahrada defile. To them, Gujarat promised plunder and passage to the sea.

panels.shot: dynamic high-angle shot from cliffside, Chaulukya and Rajput forces poised to descend

dialogue.text: But on the heights, Gujarat and its allies had already arrived. Later verses would boast of elephants and steeds surging downhill, of the Turushka line thrown into confusion.

panels.shot: cinematic wide of chaotic battlefield at the foothills, dust and motion without gore

dialogue.text: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri does not linger on detail. It records that the army marching toward Nahrwala was routed, its commander escaping with difficulty, its ranks scattered by defeat.

panels.shot: contrasting calm shot of Naikidevi in a field tent receiving news, medium close

dialogue.speaker: Messenger
dialogue.text: Devi, the Turushka host is broken. Their prince has fled the field.

panels.shot: profile close-up of Naikidevi, expression controlled, with faint relief

dialogue.text: No chronicler records her words in that moment. Yet every inscription that follows speaks of what her decision secured: the young king’s throne, the western gate, the fragile balance of power.

panels.shot: wide shot of a temple town being repaired, artisans at work, Naikidevi visiting

dialogue.text: The Kiradu record had spoken of temples harmed in earlier Turushka raids and later repaired. Victories like Kasahrada did not end that cycle, but they gave space to rebuild between storms.

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition showing later scribes carving the Sundha Hill inscription

dialogue.text: On Sundha Hill, the Jalor Chahamanas carved their boast: how they helped break the Turushka host at Kasahrada. Behind their pride stands the regent who made their gathering possible.

panels.shot: somber interior shot of Patan court years later, Naikidevi older, with grown Mularaja beside

dialogue.text: The Ghurids would return to Gujarat under Qutb al-Din Aibak in 1197, and this time they would succeed. Their first attempt, though, had already been blunted by a regent’s choice of field.

panels.shot: final reflective wide shot of the Thar route and Aravalli hills at sunset, Naikidevi’s silhouette faintly superimposed

dialogue.text: Her name survives in grants and inscriptions, not epics, yet in 1178 Naikidevi showed how power can be held: by seeing the storm early, and choosing the ground before the battle begins.
